Tide 1.1.0

  • Pin tabs: right-click a tab and choose Pin Tab. Pinned tabs stay at the start of the tab bar, show a pin instead of the close button, and come back pinned after a relaunch.
  • Closing the last tab no longer quits Tide: the window stays open with a New Tab button (or press Cmd-T).
  • Clicking anywhere in a pane now puts the keyboard on its input, not only the writing area. Selecting text by dragging still works.
  • After closing every tab, the next launch starts with one fresh tab instead of bringing back the last one you closed.
  • New Settings window (Cmd-,): choose a default folder for new tabs, new splits and the tab Tide opens at launch, or keep the current behaviour.
  • Programs like Claude Code can now copy to your clipboard through the terminal (OSC 52), so the "blocked" notice no longer appears. You can turn this off in Settings; reading the clipboard stays blocked.
  • Tide now appears in Finder's Open With menu for text, code and folders (it never becomes the default app). Opening a folder starts a new tab there.
  • New services "New Tide Tab Here" and "New Tide Window Here" in Finder's context menu and the Services menu. If they are missing, turn them on in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > Services.

Tide 1.0.2

  • The explorer now colours folders by their git state, like VS Code: yellow when something inside changed, green when it only has new files, red when it only has deletions.
  • Git state works in folders that contain several repositories, at any depth: open a workspace like ~/Developer and every repo inside is tracked.
  • Files ignored by each repository (node_modules, build output) are dimmed inside nested repos too.
  • Hidden files are shown in the explorer by default.
  • Fixed the hover highlight sticking to rows while scrolling the explorer.
  • Fixed zsh history being saved inside the app instead of your ~/.zsh_history.

Tide 1.0.1

  • Smoother tab dragging: the tab follows the pointer one to one and neighbouring tabs slide into place only when you pass their middle.
  • Fixed tabs swapping too early, tabs jumping vertically while dragged, and a tab staying visible after being dropped into a collapsed group.
  • Esc or releasing outside the window cancels a tab drag and returns the tab to its place.
  • Security hardening for dropped file names, git repositories you browse, and files opened externally.

Tide 1.0.0

  • First public release.
  • A native macOS terminal with command blocks: every command and its output is a block you can search, copy and collapse.
  • Split panes, tabs you can rename, reorder and group, and a command palette.
  • Tools panel with a file explorer, global search, a built-in editor and a git review pane.
  • Hover previews and Quick Look for files, images and links in the output.
  • Automatic updates with Sparkle (no data about your Mac is sent).
